# Program evaluation and partner forms

> [Download the Word version](Evaluation_and_Partner_Forms.docx) · This Markdown copy is generated from the DOCX. Update the DOCX, then run `python scripts/sync_documents.py --write` from the repository root. Print layout, page breaks, headers/footers, and writing-space height remain in Word.

Use these forms to improve the pilot and preserve evidence that can support the team’s outreach story. They are blank working templates. No participant counts, learning gains, quotes, or future recruitment outcomes have been invented.

### A small set of useful measures

Record unique participants, attendance at each session, dated classroom observations and final responses, a brief demonstration rubric, mentor preparation and delivery hours, and YMCA feedback. Keep a sample of code or design work with a date and team ID. Track future interest and actual follow-on participation separately.

### Responsible record keeping

The adult coordinator keeps identifiable registration and contact details in the YMCA’s approved system. Use student IDs in the teaching log. Obtain the agreed permission before collecting or publishing a photo, quote, or identifiable work. Share aggregate results in award materials and keep private records access-limited. Do not require publicity permission to participate.

### Counts that mean different things

Unique students counts each child once. Participant sessions counts one child attending one meeting. Contact hours sums actual attendance time across participants. Mentor hours counts each mentor’s actual time and distinguishes preparation from instruction. Family visitors are a separate count. Avoid adding these different measures into a single reach number.

### Evidence ownership

A high school mentor records teaching observations. The adult lead checks the records and consent status. The YMCA contact confirms dates, activities, and partner feedback. Student award writers can use approved summaries and anonymized examples. A document link alone does not establish that an activity occurred.

### Longer term follow through

Ask whether the YMCA wants a repeat cohort and what should change. Offer a future team open house through family contacts who opted in. Record actual later participation when it happens, with permission. Do not predict team recruitment success from interest ratings.

## YMCA partner feedback

Partner contact and role \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_  Date \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Please answer from your observations. A short signed email or completed form can confirm the activity. Do not supply an endorsement you do not agree with.

**1.** Which dates and activities can you confirm took place?

**2.** What community need did the program address, and who was able to participate?

**3.** What did you observe students learning or enjoying? Please give one concrete example.

**4.** What created difficulty for families, staff, or students?

**5.** Would you host another cohort? What should change first?

**6.** May the team use your feedback in its outreach documentation? Identify any wording or identifying details that must remain private.

### A truthful narrative structure

“We identified \[need\] with \[partner\]. Student mentors delivered \[actual activity\] for \[unique count\] students across \[completed sessions\]. Among \[number observed\] students, \[specific demonstrated skill and dated example\]. The partner reported \[approved feedback\]. We changed \[specific aspect\] and plan \[clearly labeled next step\].” Leave unknown fields blank until evidence exists.

### Award use

Engineering Inspiration and Impact have different evaluation processes. Use the current official FIRST pages linked in the proposal. This packet supports evidence gathering; it does not guarantee an award or replace the team’s broader story. Describe this as a community program unless it actually becomes a registered FIRST team. Do not call participants new FIRST team members merely because they attended.

### Sustainability checklist

Identify next year’s student mentor lead, retain known-good files and setup photos, make a parts replacement plan, review the eight-session sequence with the YMCA, and decide whether to repeat or expand only after evaluating the pilot.

## Family invitation and follow up draft

Use after the YMCA confirms registration details. Replace the blanks before sharing. This draft has not been sent.

MechaRAMS and the YMCA are preparing eight robotics sessions for 12 children in grades 5 and 6. Teams of three build removable attachments and course models, test robot missions, use small prepared code recipes, and explain their designs. Beginners are welcome. No home robot or prior programming experience is required.

### Optional next step after the program

“Would your family like information about a future high school robotics open house or another community STEM activity? Yes / No. Please provide your response through the YMCA’s agreed contact process.” This is an interest option, not a commitment to join the high school team.

### Student mentor reflection
